sources.openalex: https://api.openalex.org/works?search=<query> (title, abstract and full-text search where indexed); top 25 saved; no key, no email sent
sources.semantic_scholar: https://api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1/paper/search (fields title, year, venue, externalIds, abstract); exponential back-off on HTTP 429; no key
sources.crossref: https://api.crossref.org/works?query=<query>; top 20 saved. Crossref total-results counts every record matching any query term and is not a measure of topical overlap
sources.forward_citations: OpenAlex filter=cites:<work id>, all citers listed and screened by title, then abstracts read for relevant ones
sources.doi_verification: Crossref /works/<doi>: title similarity >= 0.85 after normalisation and year equal to a Crossref date; failures marked

method.screening: Queries were over-inclusive per candidate. Hits were pooled, de-duplicated by DOI or normalised title, screened by title, then by abstract (OpenAlex inverted index). Papers without an available abstract are described from title and metadata only and are marked as such.
limitations: Semantic Scholar (no API key) returned HTTP 429 for most requests even after exponential back-off. A 22-query subset was planned; 8 were attempted (1 succeeded), 4 key queries were retried with 45 s pauses (1 more succeeded), and the remaining 14 were not attempted. Only the 's2' records with a hit_count succeeded; neither returned a new precedent. Results rest mainly on OpenAlex and Crossref; the 's2' queries should be rerun with an API key before submission.
OpenAlex rejects '*' in search strings (HTTP 400); those queries were re-run with 'A star' and 'Theta star'.
Several Elsevier abstracts are not available in OpenAlex or Crossref; ScienceDirect returned HTTP 403. Their descriptions are limited to titles.
No full texts were read except the abstract of the Zenodo preprint of Schroeder, Arnold and Seyfried.
Dashes and curly quotes in titles were normalised to ASCII.

candidates.name: Escape-deadline maps
candidates.statement_as_given: For every node of the building graph, the latest time an occupant can still leave and reach an exit with accumulated FED below the incapacitation threshold, under a growing fire; computed exactly by a reverse (latest-departure) time-dependent label-setting or profile search over FIFO arrival functions combined with the dose DP, from IFC in real time, with machine-checked correctness. Output: a time-left-to-leave field over the building.
candidates.refined_statement: Define T*(v) = sup{t : some walk leaving v at t, waiting allowed, reaches an exit with X_FED <= X_crit and enters no node after its untenability time}. With a monotone hazard (local dose rate non-decreasing in time) and non-decreasing edge traversal times, a walk left earlier is never worse, so feasibility is downward closed in t and T*(v) is well defined. On the time-expanded graph, one backward induction over layers gives D(v,k), the least dose to an exit when leaving v at layer k, for all (v,k) in O(K|E|); then T*(v) = max{k : D(v,k) <= X_crit}. The field T*(v), and the margin T*(v) - RSET(v), is the deliverable. Under hard tenability windows only (no dose), T* reduces to a classical latest-departure query, which is not new; the dose constraint, the all-nodes field, the monotonicity theorem and the machine-checked proof are the contribution.

candidates.name: Pareto time-dose egress routing
candidates.statement_as_given: Bi-criteria (arrival time, FED) label-correcting search on a time-dependent network, returning the non-dominated routes.
candidates.refined_statement: Exact non-dominated (arrival time, FED) routes from one origin on the time-expanded graph; with integer time layers the time criterion is explicit in the layer, so the Pareto set at each node is the lower envelope of D(v,k) over k.

candidates.name: Two-zone fire model on the IFC room graph coupled online to lattice routing in the browser
candidates.statement_as_given: A two-zone fire model (CFAST-style) on the IFC room graph, coupled online to lattice routing in the browser.
candidates.refined_statement: Zone ODEs per room (upper-layer temperature, layer height, species) integrated in the browser, mapped to lattice nodes as time-dependent tenability, consumed by the routing layer.

candidates.name: Hierarchical routing from non-manifold topology
candidates.statement_as_given: A room/aperture graph from non-manifold topology (TopologicPy cells and apertures) over the fine lattice, with a consistent heuristic for exact search.
candidates.refined_statement: Use exact room-graph distances (lower bounds on lattice distances) as a consistent abstraction heuristic for A* on the lattice.

candidates.name: Machine-checked verification of fire-engineering correlations and egress algorithms
candidates.statement_as_given: Machine-checked (proof assistant) verification of fire-engineering correlations and egress algorithms as a methodology.
candidates.refined_statement: Lean 4 + Mathlib proofs of dimensional homogeneity for about 90 fire and tenability equations, and correctness of the egress algorithms (A*/Dijkstra, FIFO time-dependent Dijkstra, time-expanded dose DP), reported as a methodology for fire safety engineering.

candidates.name: Any-angle egress paths with certified wall clearance
candidates.statement_as_given: Any-angle egress paths with certified wall clearance on IFC-derived graphs.
candidates.refined_statement: Theta*-style any-angle search on the IFC lattice with a guaranteed minimum clearance from walls.

C1.title: A map representation of the ASET-RSET concept

doi_verification.title: A map representation of the ASET-RSET concept

C1.evidence_basis: Abstract of the authors' preprint on Zenodo (record 3949625); journal full text not read (closed access).
C1.what_it_does: Introduces ASET and RSET maps generated by a spatial evaluation of the quantities used to determine ASET and RSET from fire and evacuation model output, a difference map of the safety margin over the whole domain, and a reduction of the map to one scalar consequence measure.
C1.where_it_stops: The abstract describes a spatial post-processing of simulation output. It does not describe a route-dependent latest departure from each location, dose accumulated along the escape route, an exactness guarantee, or a machine-checked proof.
C1.closeness: closest (concept of a spatial safety-margin map)

scoring_scale.novelty: 5 = no precedent found for the core contribution; 1 = done before
scoring_scale.feasibility: 5 = days to two weeks in Studio reusing existing components; 1 = months
scoring_scale.research_value: 5 = clear contribution for a strong journal; 1 = engineering only
scoring_scale.user_value: 5 = changes decisions of designers and fire engineers directly; 1 = cosmetic

rationale.novelty: Every ingredient has a precedent (spatial ASET maps, reverse trigger computations, node safety under deterministic hazard, latest-departure routing, exposure-constrained labels), but no record found combines an all-nodes latest-departure field with a cumulative FED constraint, an exactness argument and a machine-checked proof. Two papers could not be read in full (Chen et al. 2023; Tabirca et al. 2015) and may narrow it further.
rationale.feasibility: One backward induction on the time-expanded graph, about 4.6e7 relaxations at Studio sizes (estimate from section 4.3 of the methods study, not measured). Reuses the IFC lattice, the FED equations, the time-expanded DP and the FIFO lemmas L10a, L10b, L11; new Lean work is a monotonicity lemma and DP correctness on a DAG, days to two weeks. Depends on the metric clock and FED heat model (steps 3 and 4 of section 10).
rationale.research_value: A route-aware, dose-based ASET map with a stated guarantee answers the open issue raised by map-based ASET/RSET work and the ASET/RSET critique; fits Fire Safety Journal, Fire Technology or Automation in Construction.
rationale.user_value: A time-left-to-leave field is directly readable by designers and fire engineers, compares with RSET at every location, and shows where a layout change buys time.

rationale.novelty: Bi-attribute time-varying fire egress DP (1991), exact Pareto labels with an exposure constraint (2024), time-and-dose bi-objective fire routing (2025) and generic time-dependent bicriteria algorithms (2005, 2006, 2026) exist. Only the FED criterion on an IFC lattice remains.
rationale.feasibility: Pareto label sets on a 38,000-edge lattice over 600 layers can grow large; the time-expanded form keeps it tractable but needs care.
rationale.user_value: Designers rarely act on a Pareto set; one deadline or one route is easier to use.

rationale.novelty: Zone model plus egress plus tenability coupling dates to HAZARD I (1989) and CRISP (1994); IFC-to-fire-and-evacuation and browser fire-evacuation twins exist. Novelty is in packaging only.
rationale.feasibility: Six to twelve weeks with a CFAST comparison (section 9 of the methods study).
rationale.research_value: Publishable only with validation against CFAST or experiments.
rationale.user_value: High: physical fire behaviour per room is what fire engineers expect.

rationale.novelty: IndoorGML hierarchy, IFC room-door graphs and abstraction heuristics for exact A* (Holte et al. 1996) are established; the TopologicPy source of the room graph is the only new element.
rationale.feasibility: Needs the room graph (planned) and a lower-bound proof linking room and lattice distances.
rationale.user_value: Speed and a readable room-level route; useful but not decisive.

rationale.novelty: No record found of a proof assistant applied to fire-engineering correlations, tenability or egress algorithms; neighbouring work exists for units (Isabelle/HOL), chemical physics and high-energy physics (Lean), a numerical wave-equation program (mechanised proof), reliability analysis and heat conduction (HOL) and static Dijkstra implementations. It is a transfer of method into a new domain.
rationale.feasibility: Already under way (eleven theorems proved; core set planned).
rationale.research_value: Moderate alone; stronger as the verification layer of a method paper.
rationale.user_value: Indirect: confidence for reviewers and regulators rather than a design output.

rationale.novelty: Theta*, optimal any-angle planning, the Explicit Corridor Map and exact-clearance navigation meshes cover it.
rationale.user_value: Smoother lines on screen; little effect on egress decisions.

recommendation.combine_with: C5, as the verification layer of C1 rather than a separate paper.
recommendation.method: Escape-deadline field T*(v) on the IFC lattice: backward induction on the time-expanded graph gives D(v,k), the least FED to an exit when leaving v at layer k, for all nodes and layers; T*(v) = max{k : D(v,k) <= X_crit}. Report T*(v), the margin T*(v) - RSET(v) with pre-movement as a distribution, and the route that attains it.
theorems_to_prove: Monotone hazard and non-decreasing traversal times imply that D(v,k) is non-decreasing in k, so the feasible departure times from v form a down-set and T*(v) is well defined.
Backward induction on the layered DAG equals the minimum dose over all walks with waiting (DP correctness).
Deadline extraction is correct: T*(v) is feasible and every later layer is infeasible.
Hard-window special case: T*(v) equals the latest departure of the FIFO network (links to L10a, L10b, L11).
Dimensional homogeneity of the FED increments used (L16).
recommendation.narrowed_novelty_claim: Searches of OpenAlex and Crossref (Semantic Scholar was rate-limited for most queries) on 2026-10-27 found no work that computes, for every location of a building navigation graph, the latest time an occupant can still leave and reach an exit with accumulated FED below a criterion under a time-varying fire, with an exactness guarantee and a machine-checked proof. Others stopped short of this: map-based ASET/RSET evaluates tenability quantities spatially from simulation output (Schroeder et al. 2020); trigger buffers and beat-the-wave maps compute a latest time to leave at community scale against a fire or wave arrival, without dose (Cova et al. 2005; Li et al. 2018; Mitchell et al. 2023; Priest et al. 2015); node safety under deterministic hazard spread was computed for sensor-network guidance without dose or proof (Barnes et al. 2007; Tabirca et al. 2009, 2015); latest-departure routing in a time-varying evacuation network exists for mine flooding without dose (Du et al. 2020); exposure- or temperature-constrained routes exist for single origins (Yen et al. 2020; Bi et al. 2024). The claim is the combination, not any single ingredient, and it is conditional on reading Chen et al. (2023) and Tabirca et al. (2015) in full.
